Native R batched scientific validation and irregular functional trajectory contracts

etr_native_batch.Rd

Independent Python-free R implementations of ten public functions from the published eyetrajectoriespy 1.2.0 validation.py, irregular.py and phase.py source modules. Also defines an explicit R native irregular-trajectory representation.

Usage

etr_validate_common_grid(x)
etr_validate_simplex(values, atol = 1e-7,
  python_boundary_mode = FALSE)
etr_validate_no_long_missing_runs(x, max_missing_fraction)
etr_irregular_trajectory_set(time, values, curve_ids, dimension_names,
  metadata = NULL, coordinate_system = "unknown",
  time_unit = "unknown", provenance = list(), allow_infinite_values = FALSE)
etr_from_irregular_long_native(data, curve_columns, time_column,
  value_columns = c("x", "y"), metadata_columns = NULL,
  coordinate_system = "unknown", time_unit = "unknown",
  provenance = NULL)
etr_common_overlap_interval(x)
etr_make_common_grid(x, n_time, domain = "overlap",
  start = NULL, end = NULL)
etr_resample_irregular_to_grid(x, grid, method = "linear",
  max_gap = NULL)
etr_resample_irregular_to_common_grid(x, n_time, domain = "overlap",
  method = "linear", max_gap = NULL)
etr_irregular_sampling_summary(x)
etr_phase_landmark_frame(registration)

Arguments

x

Native common-grid trajectory collection for validators; for irregular operations, an etr_irregular_trajectory_set.

values

A numeric three-dimensional simplex array for validation; a list of curve-specific sample-by-channel matrices for construction.

atol

Finite nonnegative absolute sum and negativity tolerance. NumPy-style sum comparison additionally applies relative tolerance 1e-5.

python_boundary_mode

An explicit opt-in to bounded frozen Python 1.2 coercion for validation: numeric-string or Boolean 3D arrays, complex NumPy-ndarray-style arrays (real component only), regular 3D nested scalar lists, and vacuous zero-curve/time validation. The native default keeps strict numeric-array checks; neither mode claims complete NumPy object/exception parity.

max_missing_fraction

Maximum permitted fraction of time points with at least one missing functional channel per curve, in [0,1).

time

List of finite increasing curve-specific time vectors, each at least two samples long.

curve_ids,dimension_names

Distinct nonempty string identifiers and channel names.

metadata

Optional one-row-per-curve native R data frame.

coordinate_system,time_unit

Declared spatial and temporal units.

provenance

JSON-like named native R source-audit list.

allow_infinite_values

Permit infinite sample values for the source PACE future-prediction boundary. A target forecast uses only finite history values and calibration requires a finite observation at each forecast time.

data

Long-format data frame; rows are samples.

curve_columns

One or more identifier columns.

time_column

Numeric curve-specific observation-time column.

value_columns

Numeric functional-channel columns.

metadata_columns

Optional curve-constant metadata columns.

n_time

Integer number of desired common-grid locations, at least two.

domain

"overlap" for common support or "union" for the full observed domain.

start,end

Optional explicit finite grid endpoints, supplied together.

grid

Finite strictly increasing target sample times.

method

Currently "linear" only. Python's "pchip" is explicitly rejected rather than silently approximated.

max_gap

NULL or finite positive maximum spacing that may be interpolated. Wider internal gaps remain missing.

registration

Named native R registration result with an original trajectory collection, numeric matrix observed_landmarks and numeric vector reference_landmarks.

Value

The three validation functions invisibly return NULL on success and raise descriptive errors on failure. The constructor/from-long functions return etr_irregular_trajectory_set, retaining independent time vectors, sample matrices, names, metadata and provenance. The overlap function returns a length-two numeric vector; the grid builder returns a numeric sample grid. The two resampling functions return a etr_trajectory_set with scientific gap/audit provenance. The sampling summary and landmark deviation functions return native R data frames with Python-compatible column names.

Details

Native irregular curves retain missing values and their own observation times until explicit resampling. No time shifting or extrapolation occurs. An interval longer than max_gap is masked strictly inside its endpoints. Python's PCHIP resampling method, pandas metadata index behavior and full IrregularTrajectorySet dataclass schema are not yet qualified for native R parity.

This batch adds ten identified Python-function native-R candidates, not ten fully independently certified contracts. Source-level mapping alone does not prove equivalence for every supported Python input. The 508-export parity catalog remains fail-closed.

All implementations run without a Python interpreter. Optional independent Python 1.2 numerical-oracle tests are opt-in.

Examples

times <- list(c(0, 1, 3), c(.5, 1.5, 2.5))
values <- list(matrix(c(0, 1, 3), ncol = 1),
               matrix(c(2, 3, 4), ncol = 1))
x <- etr_irregular_trajectory_set(times, values,
                                  c("A", "B"), "x")
grid <- etr_make_common_grid(x, n_time = 5L)
y <- etr_resample_irregular_to_grid(x, grid)
stopifnot(identical(dim(y$values), c(2L, 5L, 1L)))
